title: From AGI to ASI - Part 01 Reading Sample

sections.title: Opening: why AGI is not the endpoint

segments.title: Core question
segments.text_content: The paper does not only ask how AGI should be defined. It asks whether systems that reach human-level general capability can keep scaling toward ASI.

segments.title: From capability to ceiling
segments.text_content: AGI can mean human-level general intelligence across tasks, but that does not imply intelligence has reached its ceiling. Digital systems may still gain advantages in speed, replication, coordination, and search.

segments.title: System view
segments.text_content: From a systems view, ASI may not come from one model becoming stronger in isolation. It may emerge from models, tools, memory, retrieval, executors, and multi-agent structures working as a capability network.

sections.title: How the learning system handles papers

segments.title: Structured text
segments.text_content: The paper learning system first splits a source document into stable sections and segments, so notes, questions, and model results can anchor to a concrete segment in a concrete version.

segments.title: Worker role
segments.text_content: The Worker does not own core business logic. It claims tasks, prepares context, calls a model, preserves raw output, validates structured results, and writes results back through shared contracts.
